content.text:
**Bun** is a fast all-in-one JavaScript/TypeScript runtime, bundler, package manager, and test runner. It uses Apple's **JavaScriptCore** engine (instead of V8 like Node.js) and has its transpiler/runtime written in Rust (as of Bun 1.4, rewritten from Zig). This design prioritizes **fast startup**, low overhead, and high throughput, especially for scripts, HTTP servers, and developer workflows.[[1]](https://bun.com/docs/runtime)

### Startup Performance
Bun consistently starts significantly faster than Node.js:
- On Linux: A simple `hello.js` starts in **~5.1–5.2 ms** with Bun vs. **~25–27 ms** with Node.js (roughly **4–5x faster**).[[2]](https://bun.com/docs/project/benchmarking)
- On Windows (Bun 1.4): **15.5 ms** vs. Node.js **40.1 ms** (2.5x faster).[[3]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- `bun run` for package scripts: Often **~6–7 ms** vs. **~170–260 ms** for `npm run`, `yarn`, or `pnpm` (up to **25–40x faster** in some cases).[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)

Bun 1.4 further improved startup by ~50% on Linux and 2.5x on Windows compared to 1.3, with lower peak memory (e.g., ~14–17 MB for hello world vs. higher for Node).[[3]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### Runtime & Memory Improvements (Bun 1.4)
The 1.4 release (August 2026) rewrote the runtime in Rust, delivering major gains:
- **Idle CPU usage**: Reduced by up to **5x**.
- **HTTP server memory**: **13–48% lower** peak usage under load (e.g., Fastify: 233 MB → 120 MB; Express: 169 MB → 92 MB; Next.js: 397 MB → 285 MB). Bun often beats Node.js in memory efficiency.[[3]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **Production gains**: In real deployments (e.g., Claude Code or Scrydon services), CPU dropped ~50% and memory ~60% in some cases, with better stability and no memory leaks.[[5]](https://scrydon.com/insights/2026/08/21/bun-1-4-at-scrydon/)

The `--smol` flag trades some performance for even lower memory in constrained environments by running the GC more frequently.[[1]](https://bun.com/docs/runtime)

### HTTP Server & Throughput Benchmarks
Bun's `Bun.serve()` (and frameworks like Elysia/Hono on Bun) excels in many scenarios:
- **Express over HTTPS**: ~48k req/s (Bun 1.4) vs. ~25k (Node 26) and ~19k (Deno) — nearly 2x Node, with lower memory (~105 MB vs. 142 MB).[[6]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)
- **Mixed workloads** (JSON, compression, static files, DB queries): Ranked **#1** in HttpArena benchmarks, beating even some Rust servers like go-fasthttp while using far less memory (e.g., 6.1 GiB vs. 80+ GiB). Also **#2 in compression** and top 10 in JSON.[[7]](https://dev.to/fbio_reis_355b87b508598e/bun-http-server-1-in-mixed-workloads-41-in-pipelining-the-full-picture-httparena-deep-dive-4h6e)
- **Database queries** (Postgres): ~20k queries/s with Bun.sql vs. ~10k for Node/Deno.[[6]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)
- **WebSockets**: Extremely high throughput (millions of messages/sec in some tests).[[6]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)

**Caveats**: Performance varies by workload. One benchmark on Next.js-like latency-sensitive loads showed Bun with higher average latency (~246 ms) and worse tail latency (p99 ~974 ms) compared to Deno (~11–14 ms) and Node (~20 ms), suggesting it may not always win in high-latency or certain pipelined/ upload scenarios.[[8]](https://blog.platformatic.dev/bun-is-fast-until-latency-matters-for-nextjs-workloads) It ranked lower (#41) in pure pipelining tests.[[7]](https://dev.to/fbio_reis_355b87b508598e/bun-http-server-1-in-mixed-workloads-41-in-pipelining-the-full-picture-httparena-deep-dive-4h6e)

### Other Areas
- **Bundling**: Bun's bundler is often 1.75x faster than esbuild and orders of magnitude faster than Webpack/Rollup/Parcel.[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)
- **Testing**: `bun test` can be 8–13x faster than Jest/Vitest in some suites.[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)
- **FFI & Streams**: Major gains in Bun 1.4 (e.g., FFI up to ~3–4x faster; native streams and compression with high throughput and low memory).[[9]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-nz2dmgftt)
- **Real-world**: In production services and build pipelines (e.g., Next.js apps), Bun 1.4 reduces build times, CPU, and memory significantly vs. prior versions or Node.[[10]](https://appwrite.io/blog/post/announcing-bun-1-4-runtime)

### Summary
Bun shines in **startup speed**, **developer tooling**, **memory efficiency**, and **high-throughput HTTP/mixed workloads**, often outperforming Node.js and Deno in these areas (especially post-1.4). It may trail in specific latency-sensitive or niche scenarios. Benchmarks are workload-dependent—check the official `/bench` directory or tools like mitata, hyperfine, or bombardier for your use case. The project continues rapid iteration on compatibility (now passing thousands more Node tests) and performance.[[2]](https://bun.com/docs/project/benchmarking)

For the latest numbers, see the Bun blog, docs, or independent benchmarks, as results evolve with releases.
